payload.name: Past visits only when enumerating visited places
payload.description: Use when a question asks which places a person has been to, visited, or traveled to; require past completed presence and exclude plans or aspirational mentions.
content: When a question asks for locations a person 'has been to' or 'visited', list only memories that document a completed past physical presence (event with past timestamp or past-tense activity). Exclude plan memories, future-dated intentions, and aspirational statements even if the person is excited or has added them to a travel list.

Do not infer presence from reading about a place, joining a travel-related group, or discussing a place; require an explicit activity at the location (e.g., visited, toured, took a photo in, hiked in).
Before finalizing, run at least one additional search combining the person's name with activity terms that imply presence (photo, trip, visited, went, hiked), not only the verbatim query.

solves: Agents answering 'which places has X been to?' often mix future plans and aspirational reading into the list and miss implicit evidence such as photos. This skill adds a reusable rule: for past-travel questions, a location counts only with a completed event of physical presence, and searches should include activity terms that imply presence. It applies to any future enumeration of visited locations; it does not apply to questions about planned or desired destinations.
